diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check is reporting a stale or invalid all-PON failure. The stored alarm record is dated 2025-11-11, while current telemetry and live probes from 2026-09-23 show the OLT, all sampled PON-5 ONUs, and the subscriber online and operating normally.
evidence: The OLT responds successfully to ping, SNMP, and the required OID subtree, so this is not an OLT-wide device failure.
Current OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and historical telemetry are within healthy ranges.
The subscriber is online with RX -19.71 dBm and TX 2.42 dBm, both normal; optical telemetry is stable, distance is constant, and TX bias remains healthy.
All seven visible peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical readings, showing that the PON port and splitter are functioning.
The OLT population has 207 of 214 ONUs online; seven offline is below the approximately 4.85% network baseline and does not indicate an outage.
The subscriber has two sessions in 24 hours with long durations, normal traffic, valid RADIUS state, and the expected VLAN 1035, so there is no authentication, VLAN, or service fault.

The live evidence directly contradicts the stored alarm claiming all eight PONs failed. The stored health record is also stale relative to the current telemetry, identifying the monitoring check as the fault.

remediation.action: Re-run the OLT health check and clear the stale critical alarm. Investigate and repair the health-check data pipeline or scheduler so that failed-PON results cannot persist from an old run; validate all eight PONs with fresh live probes and add freshness checks for stored health records.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
